# Provider SSE regression provenance

These tests encode source-derived behavior from frozen Prodex 0.439.0 at
`433aad44bb249d5c25a231a6b06c2fa522a39a1f`:

- `crates/prodex-app/src/runtime_launch/proxy_startup/provider_sse_reader.rs`
  defines provider line/event reading, EOF and `[DONE]` ordering, JSON joining,
  separate values, accumulation, and the default 4 MiB bounds.
- `crates/prodex-runtime-proxy/src/payload_detection/sse.rs` and
  `mojo/prodex_core/sse_line.mojo` define data-field recognition and event-byte
  accounting (`data bytes + one separator byte`, rejecting only totals above
  the limit).

The fixtures are represented inline in the native unit programs and
`tests/test_provider_sse.py`. `tests/test_provider_sse_runtime.py` also runs the
driver in a disposable filesystem/network namespace with only its native
runtime libraries. Cases include byte fragmentation, exact limits, strict
UTF-8, a final CR-only event separator, and unread trailing errors after
`[DONE]`. No fixture is generated by Modex and then used as expected behavior.

The assembler returns JSON text values, not translated provider events. Its
EOF handling checks pending JSON only; provider-specific completion and
`unexpected end of stream` error envelopes require the frozen reader's state
layer and remain unfinished. The driver is test-only and is not called by
the CLI. The frozen checkout is source-only evidence here; these cases do
not claim parity against an official executable or a live provider stream.
Provider network/runtime integration and security behavior remain unverified.
